inputs.statement: For every field K, finite-dimensional K-vector space V, natural n, and independent family a:Fin n→V with dim_K V=n, the K-linear span of the range of a is all V.

hypotheses: K is a field and V is finite dimensional over K.

output.statement: For every field F, positive natural n, finite-dimensional F-vector space T with dim_F T=n, and endomorphisms C_ij∈End_F(T) indexed by i,j∈Fin n satisfying C_ij C_kl=δ_jk C_il for all indices and ∑_i C_ii=Id_T, every F-linear subspace Z⊆T preserved by all C_ij is zero or all T. Here δ_jk is 1 if j=k and 0 otherwise, and products mean composition with the right factor acting first.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary F-vector space T.
Fix arbitrary F-linear endomorphisms C_ij indexed by Fin n.
Fix an arbitrary F-linear subspace Z of T.
Choose j with C_jj w≠0 using F004.
Define u_i=C_ij z for i∈Fin n.
For the independence test fix arbitrary coefficients a:Fin n→F.
Fix an arbitrary k∈Fin n for the coefficient-isolation calculation.

argument.text: Fix F,n,T,C,Z as arbitrary data. Temporarily assume L1: n>0, T is finite dimensional of F-dimension n, C_ij C_kl=δ_jk C_il for all indices, ∑_i C_ii=Id_T, and every C_ij preserves Z. The Kronecker coefficient is 1 when its two indices coincide and 0 otherwise; products act right factor first.

produces.statement: n>0, T is finite dimensional with dim_F T=n, C_ij C_kl=δ_jk C_il for all indices, ∑_i C_ii=Id_T, and C_ij(Z)⊆Z for all indices.

argument.text: For the zero branch temporarily assume L2: Z=0. The desired disjunction Z=0 or Z=T follows by its first alternative. Discharge L2 to get the corresponding implication.

produces.statement: If Z=0 then Z=0 or Z=T.

argument.text: For the other branch assume L3: Z≠0. A subspace with no nonzero elements is the zero subspace, since it contains 0 and all its elements would equal 0. Thus L3 implies existence of a vector in Z different from zero.
Choose w∈Z with w≠0. From F001, w=∑_i C_ii w. If every summand were zero this would imply w=0, a contradiction. The index set is finite, so there exists j∈Fin n with C_jj w≠0.

produces.statement: There exists j∈Fin n with C_jj w≠0.

argument.text: Choose j from F004 and set z=C_jj w. Then z≠0. Since C_jj preserves Z and w∈Z, z∈Z. The matrix-unit relation gives C_jj z=C_jj C_jj w=C_jj w=z.

Define u_i=C_ij z for every i∈Fin n. By F001 and F005, all u_i lie in Z. For the independence test fix arbitrary coefficients a:Fin n→F and temporarily assume L4: ∑_i a_i u_i=0. Fix an arbitrary k∈Fin n and apply C_jk to this equality. Its linearity and the multiplication relation yield ∑_i a_i δ_ki C_jj z=a_k z=0. As z≠0, a_k=0: a nonzero a_k would have an inverse, giving z=0. Universally quantifying k shows every coefficient is zero. Discharge L4 and universally quantify a to prove independence of u. The resulting independence and membership facts retain only L1 and L3.

produces.statement: u:Fin n→T is F-linearly independent, and u_i∈Z for every i∈Fin n.

argument.text: Apply E002 with F,T,n,u. Finite dimensionality and dim_F T=n are in L1/F001; independence is F006. It follows that the F-linear span of u is T. Every u_i lies in Z and Z is a linear subspace, so it contains every finite linear combination, hence all of T. Thus Z=T. This conclusion does not depend on the private choices of w or j, and existential elimination removes those choices.
F007 gives the desired disjunction in the nonzero branch. Discharge L3 to get: if Z≠0 then Z=0 or Z=T.

produces.statement: If Z≠0 then Z=0 or Z=T.

argument.text: Classically Z=0 or Z≠0. Apply the two implications F002 and F008 to these exhaustive cases; both give Z=0 or Z=T. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary data F,n,T,C,Z. This is exactly the asserted output, with positivity and all matrix-unit and stability conditions retained in its antecedent.
